candidates.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen for fast agentic work
candidates.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen across the Gemini API, AI Studio, enterprise and consumer surfaces, with a one-million-token context window, four thinking levels, flat API pricing and a new Antigravity multi-model orchestrator.
candidates.what_changed: A new broadly available execution-oriented Gemini 4 tier now has a concrete access and pricing contract, while Antigravity can switch between Hydrogen and Carbon inside one session.
candidates.why_it_matters: Engineering teams can explicitly separate expensive long-horizon judgment from faster worker and verifier tasks, but Google’s speed, benchmark and safety figures remain evaluation-scoped claims.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Measure end-to-end task success, latency and total token cost on representative workflows before adopting automatic model routing, and independently test permission-boundary behavior.

evidence.rationale: Google documents availability, pricing, context length, thinking levels, orchestrator behavior and evaluation results.
evidence.independent_validation: Named external benchmarks are cited, but performance and safety results were not independently reproduced in this pass.
evidence.claim_scope: Availability and prices are established; capability, efficiency and safeguard figures remain vendor- or benchmark-scoped.

signal.rationale: A broadly available, lower-cost model plus automatic multi-model routing materially changes Gemini agent architecture choices.

deduplication.canonical_event: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Antigravity Orchestrator on 12 November.
deduplication.previous_coverage: The 12 November edition covered Carbon availability, not Hydrogen or the new automatic routing event.
deduplication.material_delta: A distinct model tier, pricing contract and routing mechanism are newly available.

candidates.title: AlphaGenome 2 predicts variant effects at cell-type resolution
candidates.summary: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaGenome 2, trained on more than 100 million cell profiles across 68 tissues to predict regulatory effects for specific cell types and states.
candidates.what_changed: The successor moves from broad tissue-level prediction to cell-type and cell-state resolution, reports nearly twice as many expression-changing variants identified, and is available through an API for non-commercial research.
candidates.why_it_matters: The release turns large single-cell atlases into a predictive system that can prioritize disease-relevant variants missed by tissue averages, while the reported gains remain first-party until broader validation.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Inspect the paper’s task definitions, held-out cell-state design and calibration before using predictions to prioritize experiments; do not treat model scores as clinical evidence.

evidence.rationale: The first-party release links the paper and documents training scale, access and comparative results.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent reproduction of the new cell-type results was identified in the bounded pass.
evidence.claim_scope: Architecture, access and reported evaluations are established as first-party research claims; biological and clinical utility remain unproven.

signal.rationale: Cell-type-specific variant prediction is a material scientific-model change with a usable research API.

deduplication.canonical_event: DeepMind announces AlphaGenome 2 and opens research API access.
deduplication.material_delta: A redesigned model adds cell-type and unseen-state predictions beyond the earlier AlphaGenome system.

candidates.title: Google tests agent anomaly monitoring on five public security benchmarks
candidates.summary: Google evaluated its private-preview Agent Anomaly Detection system on 1,774 sessions from five non-Google public benchmarks and reported that it flagged 87% of harmful instructions agents carried out.
candidates.what_changed: The September private-preview announcement now has benchmark-level evidence, including 2%–16% benign-session alert rates, weak poisoned-memory detection and sensitivity to baseline history.
candidates.why_it_matters: The study gives engineers a more honest operating envelope for asynchronous agent monitoring and shows why it cannot replace preventive tool authorization or human approval.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Treat anomaly detection as post-execution defense in depth, send complete traces, tune by tool risk and retain deterministic pre-execution controls for consequential actions.

evidence.rationale: Google publishes the benchmark set, setup, session counts, outcome definitions, false-positive ranges and failure modes.
evidence.independent_validation: The benchmarks are public and non-Google, but execution and product scoring were performed by Google on one agent model and simulated apps.
evidence.claim_scope: Results apply to the reported setup; production false-positive and detection rates may differ.

signal.rationale: The evidence exposes both useful detection rates and concrete blind spots for a production agent-security control.

deduplication.canonical_event: Google publishes public-benchmark results for Agent Anomaly Detection.
deduplication.previous_coverage: The feature entered private preview in September; no Pulse story or recent ledger covered the benchmark evidence.
deduplication.material_delta: The new report supplies 1,774-session results, false-alarm ranges and documented failure modes.

candidates.title: A2UI reaches a stable 1.0 protocol for agent-generated interfaces
candidates.summary: Google released A2UI 1.0 as the first stable version of its open generative-UI protocol, with bidirectional function calls, accessibility metadata, native renderer libraries and agent SDKs.
candidates.what_changed: The protocol now has a stable contract and cross-platform renderers for web, mobile and desktop, plus deployment evidence from named adopters and interoperability with MCP Apps.
candidates.why_it_matters: Teams can let agents describe interactive views while applications retain native components, data binding and approval surfaces instead of accepting arbitrary model-written UI code.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Evaluate the protocol boundary, component allowlist, server-side binding and function-call authorization separately from the model that composes the view.

evidence.rationale: The release documents the stable protocol, renderer and SDK surface, partner implementations and current version limits.
evidence.independent_validation: Named adopters provide deployment context, but security, latency and portability were not independently tested in this pass.
evidence.claim_scope: Protocol and library availability are established; reliability and performance claims remain first-party.

signal.rationale: A stable cross-platform protocol changes how agent-generated UI can be bounded and embedded.

deduplication.canonical_event: Google releases the first stable A2UI protocol and SDK set.
deduplication.material_delta: Version 1.0 adds a stable contract, bidirectional calls, accessibility and production renderer coverage.

candidates.title: AWS gives AgentCore a direct signed Web Search API
candidates.summary: AWS launched a direct Web Search API for Bedrock AgentCore that returns current cited results through a signed API call without requiring an AgentCore Gateway or MCP client.
candidates.what_changed: Developers can call search from AWS SDKs, the CLI or AgentCore Python SDK and use existing AWS credentials, while the prior gateway path remains available for shared platform policy.
candidates.why_it_matters: The API removes infrastructure from simple retrieval workflows but shifts search policy, result validation and prompt-injection controls into the calling application.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Choose the direct API only when application-owned policy is sufficient; preserve provenance, sanitize retrieved content and constrain downstream tool authority.

evidence.rationale: AWS documents the launch, invocation paths, SDK versions, authentication model and gateway comparison.
evidence.independent_validation: The endpoint was not independently exercised during this pass.
evidence.claim_scope: API availability and integration surface are established; result quality and operational behavior remain vendor-scoped.

signal.rationale: A direct signed search primitive materially simplifies current-information access for AgentCore applications.

deduplication.canonical_event: AWS launches the direct AgentCore Web Search API.
deduplication.material_delta: Search no longer requires a gateway target and MCP client for application-owned use cases.

candidates.title: Microsoft publishes measured outcomes from forward-deployed AI projects
candidates.summary: Microsoft reported named forward-deployed projects, including Northern Trust onboarding data preparation falling from two and a half weeks to three days at 96.5% first-pass quality and KT network issue detection falling from more than ten minutes to two or three.
candidates.what_changed: A portfolio report now supplies concrete deployment architecture and measured operating outcomes for multiple named customers rather than generic adoption claims.
candidates.why_it_matters: The cases show where agent systems create value when embedded in existing tools with monitoring and human control, while results remain vendor-selected and not independently audited.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Demand task-level baselines, quality gates, human authority boundaries and post-launch outcome tracking before generalizing from a successful pilot.

evidence.rationale: Microsoft names customers, systems, baselines, measured outcomes and human-control mechanisms.
evidence.independent_validation: The examples are vendor-selected case reports and the metrics were not independently audited in this pass.
evidence.claim_scope: Reported project outcomes are attributable to Microsoft and customers; causal and general claims are not inferred.

signal.rationale: Concrete deployment metrics and control designs offer stronger practice evidence than an adoption announcement.

deduplication.canonical_event: Microsoft publishes measured outcomes from named Frontier Company deployments.
deduplication.material_delta: New named results include time, quality and detection-latency baselines.

candidates.title: Artificial agents lower adoption thresholds in social-contagion experiments
candidates.summary: A peer-reviewed study repeated two human choice experiments with five language models and found systematically lower adoption thresholds for artificial agents; calibrated simulations produced higher total adoption even with a modest agent share.
candidates.what_changed: The paper supplies empirical evidence that delegating choices to agents can change diffusion dynamics rather than merely automate individual decisions.
candidates.why_it_matters: Organizations deploying decision agents may alter group behavior and feedback loops because model agents respond differently to social proof, though simulations do not establish real-world population effects.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Test agent decision thresholds and correlated behavior before placing automated actors into recommendation, policy or market systems with network effects.

evidence.rationale: The peer-reviewed open-access paper reports two experiments, five models and calibrated simulations with methods and supplementary material.
evidence.independent_validation: Peer review is established; no independent replication was identified.
evidence.claim_scope: The result concerns experimental adoption thresholds and calibrated simulations, not observed real-world contagion caused by deployed agents.

signal.rationale: The result is an unexpected human-scale consequence of delegated agent decisions and fits the pilot Curious lane.

deduplication.canonical_event: Peer-reviewed study reports lower adoption thresholds across five LLM agents.
deduplication.material_delta: This is an eligible seven-day catch-up item not present in the 6–12 November archive or ledgers.

watchlist.title: Rackspace and Together AI plan dedicated GB300 inference infrastructure
watchlist.summary: Rackspace and Together AI announced a multiyear agreement for dedicated GB300 NVL72 inference infrastructure and a separate non-binding go-to-market exploration.
watchlist.what_changed: The companies named the hardware and operating split, but deployment is planned for 2027 and remains subject to conditions.
watchlist.reason: The engineering consequence depends on financing, deployment and a live customer service; the separate go-to-market letter is non-binding.
promote_when: Financing closes and production capacity, location, service availability or measured inference results become concrete.

watchlist.title: Researchers frame AI slop as a community judgement
watchlist.summary: A Nature Human Behaviour comment argues that unwanted AI content should be studied as a social judgement rather than a detection category.
watchlist.what_changed: The comment proposes a governance framing but does not report a new empirical dataset or intervention result.
watchlist.reason: The idea fits the pilot Curious lane, but publication would be premature without empirical measurement or a concrete platform-policy event.
promote_when: A dataset, comparative community study or implemented governance policy tests the proposed framing.

exclusions.title: AWS describes an Agent Development Lifecycle
exclusions.summary: AWS published an evaluation-driven lifecycle guide with a reproducible reference implementation and one measured example.
exclusions.what_changed: The article packages existing evaluation-driven development practices into an AWS-oriented delivery method.
exclusions.reason: Useful implementation guidance belongs in the independent Tools & Guides lane; it is not a distinct Daily News product or research event.

exclusions.title: GitHub publishes a practical agent-skills guide
exclusions.summary: GitHub explained how to package repeatable engineering procedures as agent skills across hosts.
exclusions.what_changed: The guide adds practical examples but no distinct protocol release, measured deployment or new compatibility event.
exclusions.reason: Evergreen procedural guidance remains in the independent Tools & Guides lane and does not qualify under the Daily News rubric.

exclusions.title: ChatGPT Enterprise appears in AWS Marketplace
exclusions.summary: OpenAI made ChatGPT Enterprise purchasable through AWS Marketplace using existing AWS billing relationships.
exclusions.what_changed: The procurement path is new but adds no technical capability or governance integration beyond the previously recorded event.
exclusions.reason: The 11 November ledger already retained this exact procurement event on watch; no material delta exists.
